newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on exports, Cargill Inc buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on exports, Cargill Inc buying.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on bullish input from USDA's weekly export inspections plus aggressive buying by key commercial Cargill Inc, traders said.
"Cargill a buyer of wheat kept the market honest today. They bought about seven million wheat but what it's all about remains to be seen," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Cargill bought five million bushels of July, and one million each of March and May plus the firm bought one million bushels of KCBT July wheat, traders said.
Nearby months found support from a USDA weekly report.
"Export inspections were better than expected on everything and that firmed the market a little but it's pretty quiet," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

USDA early Tuesday said U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended January 16 totaled 14.334 million bushels. The tally was above the 12.111 million bushels reported inspected the previous week and above trade expectations which ranged from eight million to 13 million bushels.
Wheat closed unchanged to 5-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-3/4 at $3.82-1/4 a bushel.
But wheat exports so far in the 1996-97 marketing year at 713.837 million bushels remained well behind the previous marketing year's pace at 821.349 million.
Wheat futures remained subdued on a reminder this week about the large supply of wheat worldwide, traders said.
The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) this week boosted to 23 million tonnes its outlook for 1996-97 Australian wheat production. The previous estimate was for 21.5 million tonnes.
In addition to the outright commercial buying in wheat, commercial spreading was noted with Continental Grain doing two million bushels of March/July, traders said.
Continental also was an outright seller of one million July, LIT America sold two million bushels each of March and July and ADM Investor Services sold 1.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 19,000 contracts, slightly below the 19,497 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc bought 125 May $3.90 calls at six cents and LIT America sold 75 March $3.90 calls at four cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,000 contracts, below the 6,983 traded Monday.
